title: Supergene validation: A model-based protocol for assessing the accuracy of non-model-based supergene methods
author: Adams, Castoe

steps.title: Infer individual gene trees
steps.instruction: For each locus in the dataset, infer a maximum‑likelihood gene tree and obtain bootstrap support values using a phylogenetic program of choice.

steps.title: Construct supergenes
steps.instruction: Use a non‑model‑based supergene method (e.g., statistical binning) to build an incompatibility graph from the gene‑tree bootstrap supports and partition the loci into a non‑overlapping set of supergenes.

steps.title: Validate with Likelihood Ratio Tests
steps.instruction: Run the program Concatepillar to perform hierarchical likelihood‑ratio tests (LRTs) on each inferred supergene, testing models containing 1 to n trees (where n is the number of loci in the supergene). Compute LRT as L(D|Mtrue)/L(D|Mfalse) or log‑LRT = logL(D|Mtrue) – logL(D|Mfalse). Accept the supergene as true if the best‑fit model includes a single tree (n = 1); otherwise reject it as a false supergene (n ≥ 1).

steps.title: Validate with Tree Topology Tests
steps.instruction: For each locus within a supergene, obtain its ML gene tree and the overall supergene tree, then perform a Shimodaira‑Hasegawa (SH) test (implemented in RAxML) to compare the two topologies. If any locus rejects the supergene topology, label the supergene as false; if all loci fail to reject, label it as true. (Other TTTs such as the AU test may be used similarly.)

steps.title: Validate with Bayes Factors
steps.instruction: Estimate marginal likelihoods for two competing models using a Bayesian phylogenetic program (e.g., BEAST or MrBayes): (i) a “true supergene” model where all loci share a single tree, and (ii) a “false supergene” model where each locus has its own tree. Approximate marginal likelihoods with Harmonic Mean, Stepping‑Stone, or Thermodynamic Integration methods. Compute Bayes Factor BF = P(Mtrue|D) / P(Mfalse|D). A BF favoring the true‑supergene model indicates validation; a BF favoring the false‑supergene model indicates a false positive.

steps.title: Summarize validation results
steps.instruction: Aggregate the outcomes of the LRT, SH‑test, and Bayes‑Factor analyses across all supergenes. Calculate the proportion of false supergenes (e.g., >93 % false supergenes were reported for the avian statistical‑binning analysis). Compare concordance among the three validation approaches and report overall performance of the supergene method.
